supported.title: Counter
supported.says: State and two events: the smallest interactive page.

supported.title: Stopwatch
supported.says: A capability in use: a stopwatch that reads `clock.now()`, declared with `requires Clock;`, and ticks every 100 ms with `every 100 Tick;`.

supported.title: Search with cancellation
supported.says: A search whose request is superseded by the next keystroke; `Ok`, `Err` and `Cancelled` each have a view (the service is simulated).

supported.title: Notes that survive a reload
supported.says: `Storage`: a note saved in the browser's `localStorage` and read back after a reload.

supported.title: Composed components
supported.says: Several instances of one component, each with its own state, kept across the parent's re-render.

supported.title: Result with match
supported.says: A `Result` that is `Ok` or `Err`, and a `match` that must cover both.

supported.title: Machine console
supported.says: A table with search, sort, paging and a button per row, over 23 sample machines in a static file; the saved list shows offline. Sending a setpoint needs a service, so here it reports an error.

supported.title: Screens at their own URLs
supported.says: `route`, `NavLink` and `router.go`: a list and a detail, each at its own URL fragment (`#/items/valve`). The browser's Back button works, a reload stays on the page, and "Open on its own" gives a link you can share.

supported.title: Choosing a file
supported.says: `FileField`: a native file picker. The page reads a text file (UTF-8 only, at most 100,000 bytes, `.txt` or `.csv`), shows its name, size and first line, and sends it with `net.post`. On this static site there is no service to send to, so Send reports the refusal.

supported.title: Charts
supported.says: `Chart`: a line and a bar chart drawn as SVG from one list of numbers, with a text alternative a screen reader reads and a collapsed data table. The chart draws the last 1,000 values and the table lists the last 200; "Double them" shows the limit.

supported.title: Languages and right to left
supported.says: One screen in English, Arabic and Russian. The texts are catalogs the compiler checks (a missing key or a plural form a language lacks is refused); numbers, percent, dates and times are written from tables, not `Intl`. The page starts in the browser's language, switches with a button, and turns right to left for Arabic.

supported.title: Reordering a list
supported.says: `SortList`: drag a row by its handle (mouse, pen or finger), or move it with its up and down buttons from the keyboard; the focus follows the row, a live region says where it went, and the page is not redrawn under a drag. The program owns the list and accepts a move with one line, `move(tasks, from, to)`.

supported.title: A map with its list
supported.says: `Map`: the tiles of an address the program writes (here a folder of stand-in tiles beside this page; the compiler has no default tile host and this page asks nobody else for anything), the places pinned over them, the same places as a list nearest first (the list is what a screen reader reads), and the credit under the map. The map is centred on the middle of the tile, so a tile server learns the tile and no more.

soon.title: Native shell and push on mobile
soon.missing: Push notifications and background work. Whether an installed web page can do them is not measured (device tests are #65), so whether a native shell is needed is an open decision.

probe.contains: Native shells (levels 1 and 2), a React Native comparison, push
